project.name: Pixel Art Workbench
project.identity: A local-first pixel asset workbench for cutout, palette-controlled underpainting, and canonical integer scaling.
project.audience: Artists and developers converting visual references into controlled inputs for authored pixel work.
project.core_loop: Import a reference, create or import its alpha cutout, apply asset-family palette and material budgets, inspect deterministic diagnostics, export a replayable bundle, finish one canonical sprite in Aseprite, and derive exact integer display scales.
project.north_star: Automated preparation saves repair time while the final pixels remain visibly authored.

scope.purpose: Provide a reusable image-to-pixel production bridge with inspectable, reproducible output.
scope.boundary: The tool owns local preprocessing and export bundles; the artist owns final authorship and Aseprite owns editing.

mvp.definition: A tested browser workbench and CLI sharing one deterministic core, with reversible cutouts, palette locking, region control, diagnostics, replayable exports, canonical scaling, and Aseprite handoff.

complete_product.definition: The MVP validated across several real art cleanup sessions, with any recurring manual work promoted into bounded tools.

outcomes.name: A source and recipe produce an inspectable, replayable underpainting bundle.

layers.intended: The user requested a standalone tool that provides value beyond one website.
layers.planned: PRODUCT.md and docs/PRD.md define the underpainting boundary and acceptance criteria.
layers.implemented: Shared processing core, reversible local alpha-mask workflow, asset profiles, locked palettes, browser worker, canonical scale exports, CLI resize command, and Aseprite handoff are present.
layers.verified: Formatting, typecheck, lint, 14 unit and CLI tests with 92.63 percent statement coverage, dead-code analysis, production build, external-Chrome desktop/mobile cutout and export interaction, CLI resize output, and installed-Aseprite handoff reopening pass. Repeated real cleanup sessions remain future complete-product evidence.
